title: Big etale higher direct images commute with stack base change
statement: Work in the universes and small-skeleton convention of [def-weil-size-convention]. For a scheme $S$ [def-pc-scheme] and an algebraic stack $\mathcal Z/S$ [def-sfb-algebraic-moduli-stack], its big etale site has all objects and arrows of the fibred category in [def-sfb-stack-quasi-coherent-algebra], with coverings lying over jointly surjective etale scheme maps. Its structure sheaf is $\mathcal O_{\mathcal Z}(z)=\Gamma(U,\mathcal O_U)$ for $z$ over $U$. Use module sheaves [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category]. For $h:\mathcal A\to\mathcal Z$, direct image has value $(h_*N)(z)=\Gamma(\mathcal A\times_{\mathcal Z}U,N|_{\mathcal A\times_{\mathcal Z}U})$; restrictions are induced by base change, and pullback of a module along a stack morphism means precomposition. Higher direct images are computed by injective resolutions in all module sheaves [def-sp-injective-resolutions]. Let $f:\mathcal X\to\mathcal Y$ and $b:\mathcal Y^{\prime}\to\mathcal Y$ be arbitrary morphisms of algebraic stacks over $S$. Form $\mathcal X^{\prime}=\mathcal Y^{\prime}\times_{\mathcal Y}\mathcal X$, with projections $a:\mathcal X^{\prime}\to\mathcal X$ and $f^{\prime}:\mathcal X^{\prime}\to\mathcal Y^{\prime}$, using [def-sfb-stable-pointed-moduli-groupoids]. For every module sheaf $F$ on $\mathcal X$, placed in degree zero, for every $i\geq0$ the canonical comparison $b^*R^if_*F\xrightarrow{\sim}R^if^{\prime}_*(a^*F)$ is an isomorphism. Here all sheaves remain on the big etale sites, and both pullbacks are precomposition. No representability, smoothness, flatness, qcqs or quasi-coherence hypothesis is imposed.

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-stack-big-etale-derived-base-change] to the given $2$-Cartesian square and $F[0]$. Its hypotheses are exactly the big etale module-site conventions in the statement. It gives the canonical natural isomorphism $\beta:b^*Rf_*F\xrightarrow{\sim}Rf^{\prime}_*(a^*F)$ and states that $b^*$ and $a^*$ are exact and act termwise on complexes.

Fix $i\geq0$. For a complex $K$ of modules on $\mathcal Y$, put $Z^i=\ker d_K^i$ and $B^i=\operatorname{im}d_K^{i-1}$. Exactness of $b^*$ from [lem-sfb-stack-big-etale-derived-base-change] identifies the cycles and boundaries of the termwise complex $b^*K$ with $b^*Z^i$ and $b^*B^i$, and identifies its quotient with $b^*(Z^i/B^i)$. Hence $b^*H^i(K)\cong H^i(b^*K)$, compatibly with maps of complexes. This also holds on derived objects: the formula sends quasi-isomorphisms to quasi-isomorphisms, so it can be computed on any representing complex. Apply this to $K=Rf_*F$. By the injective-resolution definition, $H^i(Rf_*F)=R^if_*F$ and $H^i(Rf^{\prime}_*(a^*F))=R^if^{\prime}_*(a^*F)$. Thus $H^i(\beta)$, preceded by the displayed cohomology identification, is precisely the canonical comparison $b^*R^if_*F\to R^if^{\prime}_*(a^*F)$. It is invertible: applying the cohomology functor to $\beta^{-1}$ gives the inverse of $H^i(\beta)$. This proves the assertion in every degree, without any further geometric hypothesis.
